courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: Germany Today
courses.description: Germany was a once divided nation with complex historical background and rich culture which continuously attracts international interest. This course investigates trends and developments in contemporary German culture and society from a cross-cultural perspective, taking into consideration the historical events of different generations in Germany. Students will be encouraged to compare and critically analyze the reflections about Germany and their own society. The course content will be presented by up-to-date audiovisual materials. No knowledge of German is required.
courses.learning_outcomes: The aim of this course is to let students explore different aspects of German culture and society and make them think about the source of behaviour, customs and attitudes, while comparing with Hong Kong and Chinese behaviours. The famous German poet Goethe included in his concept of culture clothing and food, history and philosophy, art and science, children’s games and sayings, climate and landscapes, economy and literature, political and private life. Although the course can not cover all aspects, it will give students an idea about German mentality and ways of thinking and refer them back to their own background. One needs to be aware of one’s own background to discover the identity of the other.

courses.description: (Please read the Study Scheme Note.) This is a summer intensive German language course for beginners, covering the full syllabus of GERM1000 and 2000.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken GERM1000,2000,2001,3000,3001,3002,3050,3051 or 4001
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, you will be able to demonstrate basic communication skills in German such as

 greetings,

 introducing yourself and others,

 exchanging basic personal information with others in a social gathering,

 communicating about issues related to the language course,

 ordering in a coffee shop and paying the bill,

 exchanging information about cities, countries and languages,

 describing geographical locations,

 describing and commenting on apartments,

 arranging a meeting with someone (private and official appointments),

 telling the time,

 talking about professions,

 giving directions.

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: German Conversation
courses.description: This course aims to enhance students’ oral communication skills in German. Through selected student-oriented stimuli and topics related to social issues and contemporary affairs, students will practice the expression and exchange of personal views and ideas. Classroom activities may include in-class activities such as dialogue, role-play, narration, speech, group discussion, debate and multimedia activities. Emphasis will be placed on oral practice and an interactive learning environment with a view to helping students build confidence and develop fluency in using the language, to speak spontaneously in social interaction and acquire conversational techniques commonly used in a German-speaking environment.
courses.learning_outcomes:
This course is designed to help you strengthen and expand your conversational skills.

To broaden and improve your capacity in German, this course focuses on the particular subset of

language skills that are fundamental to conversation. Specifically, you will:

- Improve your ability to engage in spontaneous oral discussion on basic themes and to

respond appropriately in context-specific conversational settings

- Expand and personalize your active vocabulary knowledge in common areas of

conversation

- Improve your listening comprehension skills and further your ability to understand spoken

language.

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: German for Professional Communication
courses.description: The course aims at introducing the basic features of spoken and written business-related and official German language use. Through different types of activities that enhance reading, listening, speaking and writing skills, the students will be able to handle different kinds of business-related and official situations in German confidently. Emphasis is put on the language use of German in genuine professional occasions such as telephone communication, reading and writing official letters, reading job offers, submitting job application, and preparing and attending job interviews.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:
- have attained and increased the functional German language abilities in business-related and official contexts.
- understand oral and written business-related and official messages in German.
- make up oral and written messages of business-related and official communication in German.
- be able to respond to a direct exchange of information on familiar and routine business-related and official matters in German.
- understand job ads and make up proper application documents.
- be able to successfully conduct a job interview in German.
courses.course_syllabus:
Introduction into spoken German business language I
- Introducing yourself
- Conducting small talk
- Expressing politeness
Grammatical/Cultural Phenomena:
- Use of in/formal “you” in German-speaking countries
- Subjunctive

Introduction into spoken German business language II
- Conducting phone calls formally/informally
- Basic enquiries
- Simple business-related role plays
Grammatical/Cultural Phenomena:
- Appropriate behavior on the tele-phone in German-speaking countries
- Use of questions, subjunctive and imperative for addressing enquiries

Introduction into written German business language
- Features of official language (structures, lexis, etc.)
- Reading and understanding basic features of simple official letters/e-mails
- Making up simple official letters and e-mails (complaint, enquiry, …)
Grammatical/Cultural Phenomena:
- Introduction of passive sentences
- Noun-verb-combinations as part of official language
- Appropriate creation of official letters in German-speaking countries

Job ads and application
- Reading and understanding basic features of job ads
- Making up job applications
- Making up CVs
Grammatical/Cultural Phenomena:
- Gender-aspects of job ads
- Coordinating and subordination conjunctions as a means of text coherence
- Introduction of simple past tense

Job interview
- Understanding basic features of job interviews in German-speaking countries
- Preparing for a job interview
- Conducting a job interview
- Dealing with difficult situations during the interview
Grammatical/Cultural Phenomena:
- In/appropriate questions during job interviews in German-speaking countries

courses.course_syllabus:
GERM3051

This course consists of six units: *Länder und Landschaften* (Regions and Landscapes), *Familie* (Family), *Es war einmal*
(Once upon a Time), *Feiern in Deutschland* (Celebrating in Germany), *DDR Erinnerrungen* (GDR Memories) and *Von*

Schlager to Punk (From “Schlager” to Punk)

| Topic / Unit | Main texts | Speech acts | Vocabulary and Grammar | Cultural knowledge and cultural comparisons |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit 1 Länder und Landschaften Regions and Landscapes | - Official websites of German Bundesländer - Photos with captions from travel sites - Poems by Theodor Storm | - Describing landscape, nature, scenery - Discussing interplay between notions of place and self - Talking about location | - Adjective endings - Vocabulary and phrases related to describing geographical location and features of nature and scenery - Preposition with correct case for describing location | - Geography and regional diversity of Germany - Portrayal of landscape and scenery in various media - Landscape/nature associated to “home” and its expressive thematization in (German) poetry |
| Unit 2 Familie Familie | - Movie: Jenseits der Stille - Various graphs with statistical material related to the topic of family | - Discussing family relationships and family roles including issues of upbringing and role models - Discussing duties, rights and wishes of young people - Expressing own opinion | - Language related to describing relationships, family life and upbringing - Past tense of *haben*, *sein* and modal verbs - Establishing connections between cause and consequence through subordinate clauses with *weil* and *wenn* - Expressing temporal location with als | - The concept of family in Germany and Hong Kong: similarities and differences in terms of roles and values - Aspects of values in childhood and upbringing on personal and societal level - Appreciation of film as a cultural product |

| Unit 3: Es war einmal... Once upon a Time | - Fairy tale by the Grimm brothers - Alternative versions of fairy tale (in the form of short film and photo/picture) | - Telling and retelling the plot of a story - Comparing and contrasting alternative story versions | - Simple past tense (regular and irregular verbs) - Discourse markers for establishing chronology (conjunctions, adverbs of time) - Vocabulary and phrases for identifying and describing prototypical aspects of a fairy tale | - Fairy tales as reflection of temporally and culturally situated models and values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit 4 Feiern in Deutschland Celebrating in Germany | Interviews concerning individual traditions when celebrating birthdays <http://www.kaleidos.de/allta>g/rituale/geb04.htm Article on the subject of basic manners when dining <http://www.lecker.de/deko/di>nner/artikel-456654-dinner/Tisch-Knigge-Alle- wichtigen-Tischmanieren-auf-einen-Blick.html Articles on different holidays and traditions <http://www.kaleidos.de/allta>g/rituale/deindex.htm | Describing rituals and traditions Reporting about related personal experiences Comparing and contrasting rituals of different locations | Passive voice Reflexive verbs Discourse markers for expressing comparison and contrast Vocabulary and phrases related to describing typical events taking place during celebrations | Significant traditions and celebrations of the German speaking countries The cultural specificity of customs and habits during social gatherings |
| Unit 5 DDR Erinerrungen GDR Memories | Graphic novel: “*Drüben”* | Defining the meaning of typical and significant GDR/divided Germany- related terms Describing and discussing relations between personal life and society Hypothesizing on one’s own imaginary choices and actions | Relative clauses (with prepositions) Prepositions for expressing causes and consequences The genitive case Conjunctive mood for conditional and hypothetical statements Vocabulary and phrases related to German history and aspects of life in the GDR | Coming to terms with the divided Germany as a significant and defining feature of German history Autobiographical accounts of life in the divided Germany as expressions of ‘working through’ the past on both individual and societal level. |

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: German through Fairy Tales
courses.description: This course is a combination of content and language skills learning. Making use of folk tales, such as Grimm's fairy tales, legends and literary fairy tales, students will enrich their understanding of the German language as well as their knowledge about fairy tales and German culture. The tales taught will be read in simplified versions in German.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students should have achieved the following learning outcomes:
• Categorizing and understanding folk tales, legends and literary fairy tales
• Understanding the structures and symbolism of tales
• Talking about tales using relevant vocabulary
• Dramatizing a tale
courses.course_syllabus:
| **Unit** | **Topic** | **Grammar** | **Speech acts/activities** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Little Red Riding Hood | Adjective declensions, simple past | Role-play |
| 2 | Sleeping Beauty | Simple past, weil-obwohl, discourse markers for chronology | Using song and motion to describe a tale, discussing the meaning of a tale |
| 3 | Grimm’s Brothers | Simple past | Agreeing and disagreeing |
| 4 | Rapunzel | Future Tense, wenn, als, wann, Verbs in Dative Case | Retelling a tale Discussing symbolism |
| 5 | Legend: The Pied Piper | Verbs with prepositions | Describing pictures |
| 6 | Literary Fairy Tale: The Little Mermaid | Comparative and superlative, final clauses | Discussing a critique |

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: Special Topics in German
courses.description: This course aims at furthering students' understanding of selected area(s) of German language, literature or culture. Topics will vary from year to year. Offerings with different subtitles can be taken up for credit, up to a maximum of two times.
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the end of this course, students demonstrate the ability to:

- undertake projects that integrate the insights of language and culture studies.

- discuss and analyse language phenomena, literary productions or cultural representations of German.

- make use of their linguistic, literary or cultural knowledge to critically assess and evaluate productions and representations in German language, literature and culture.

However, students cannot take courses with the same course code more than once in a single term.

courses.title: German VII
courses.description: This course builds on the knowledge acquired through previous German language courses. It aims at leading students to a proficiency level comparable to the threshold at B1 of the Common European Framework for Languages (CEFR), becoming “independent users” of German. To achieve this goal, students will be encouraged to work with a communicative approach through independent or collaborative work with their peers. At the end of this course, students will have mastered most of the important grammar features of German and be able to communicate effectively in a wide range of everyday situations and a number of professional contexts. They will be able to use their oral and written language skills to relate to, reflect on and evaluate past and current issues involving the German-speaking societies.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, the student should be able to:
• understand the main points of information in conversations and texts on familiar matters relating to work, school and leisure time, etc. when clear, standard language is used,
• deal with most situations typically encountered when travelling in German-speaking countries,
• express yourself simply and coherently when talking about familiar topics and areas of personal interest,
• report on experiences and events, describe dreams, hopes and ambitions as well as make short statements and explanations.
